questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The reputition and technical background of the Univerisity meant alot. As a landscape architect i was also curious about water management  in the Netherlands. Compared to KU the technical knowledge the university has, was a very important factor aswell. Otherwise i did not know a lot about the university other than it was very good within the field of engineers which also spoke to me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good university, so many facilities and resources. Very friendly people aswell. It was nice to experience a larger university with one campus and not like in Copenhagen where all campus are split out. That also made the camps environement really nice since you met people from different fields of studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy and accessible! Their website is very easy to navigate and all the information is provided there. Even if its not, help is easy to get from them via mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The introduction program was a great assistance towards setteling down. Then i had a introduction to the machine hall they have, aswell as the woodwork lab and CAM-lab. I also had a tour around the campus aswell as the architecture faculty.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university has a partnership with a housing company which made it very easy to find accomodation. It does require that you pay a fee for that service. It was also a bit stressfull the service as many people payed for it. Everyone wanted the best accomodation, but there was enough for everyone. Otherwise housing can be a problem in Delft, so i recommend that you choose the service.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Delft it was not that bad. I was lucky to only live 200 meters from my faculty. But if you live in Delft, transportation is no problem. You can even live in Rotterdam or the Hague. The trains go all the time and are very accessible and easy to navigate.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They were very quick at answering on mail if i had any questions. Otherwise their website was easy to follow and navigate. I had no choices in choosing courses, so it was very straight forward.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Quick answering on emails was a great help and also that their website was easy to navigate.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successfull, as said i had no choices in terms of courses, so i got all the courses, which is also the ones i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of deadlines, read closely the information on their website, dont hesitate with asking stupid questions on mail they are really friendly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was good and challenging. It was more technical than here in Copenhagen, so my prior experience in Rhino was nice but not a must. They also have a lot of model making as part of the education, which was very nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: As said more technical and a lot more model making

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Model making is expensive, transport is more expensive than i thought, especially my bike. I had a cheap one so i needed to pay for repairs aswell.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than i had thought. Bike parts for repair. Model making parts aswell.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At "X" they have everything. It the schools social hub for sports, it has a canteen and a lot of different sports and activites you can go to. With a plus subscription you can go for the fitness aswell. its a bit outside the city of Delft but close to the southern part of Campus. I thought it was a bit expensive, so i chose to go climbing outside of campus. Also there were a lot of initatives among the masters. The faculty bar is also nice and had several different events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Drinking beer at bouwpub, climbing and socialising. Also go to the canal tours in Delft, it gives a nice historical view on the city. Just experiencing Delft and also going to Rotterdam and The Hague. Its also nice to go these places with people, its a good way of socialising and gathering people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Rotterdam or the Hague as you have more time here. Gather some people that also would like to go.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, the Netherlands and Denmark is very alike. If you are from Copenhagen, be aware that they are biking style is a lot more chaotic and doesnt follow any rules.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to bouwpub and drink beer, and get to know your classmates, go to rotterdam or the hague, find a sport you like and start. The rowing club looked really fun aswell, but otherwise climbing is a nice activity where you also are able to talk alot.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The biking was a bit frustrating, all the streets in the inner city are mixed use. Its just about getting used to it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness and openness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy it 
Participate as much as possible
Use all the resources they have

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have a good computer or buy a new one. You can buy one through university, its a really good opportunity to upgrade your computer.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning and friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coming back from the christmas break was a bit tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
